newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Proton says current yen level okay.
newsitem.headline: Proton says current yen level okay.

text.p: Malaysian carmaker Proton said on Friday the current trading range of the Japanese yen is within its expectations, but a surge in the yen could cause big problems for the company.

"We are within our budget as long as the yen stays at about these levels...unless there is a massive appreciation," Proton chairman Saleh Sulong told reporters after releasing the company's earnings for 1996/97.
When asked how he would define a large depreciation, he said: "If it was far in excess of 230 yen."
The ringgit closed Kuala Lumpur trading on Friday at 219.84/220.12.
Saleh said Proton had taken hedging measures against fluctuations in the yen.
"We have taken adequate measures in our hedging and forward contracts to ensure we will achieve our results according to our target," he said.
Proton is exposed to fluctuations in the yen/ringgit exchange rate as a large proportion of its components are imported from Japan.
Saleh said the company's exposure to foreign exchange fluctuations currently stood at between at 20 and 30 percent of component costs.
Proton's chief executive officer Tengku Mahaleel Tengku Ariff added that around 80 percent of Proton's engine components were now sourced locally.
Saleh said the company achieved a "double digit decrease in costs" in the year to March 31, 1997 year.
